rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or other decisions, including refusing to rent, demanding higher deposits or rent, or refusing to add family members. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.key_value: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.status_basis: Page states Berkeley City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; it is in the municipal code.

exempt_if.text: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

coverage.summary: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley with respect to current and prospective tenants.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units, lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8 cases, owner move-back rental agreements, and existing tenants subletting or adding roommates.

rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
